workflows.name: Storage Facility Daily Operations, Housekeeping & Maintenance Management

Automation Opportunity: - IoT temp/humidity monitoring → auto-alert; CMMS PM auto-generation; tenant self-service maintenance request
Controls: - CTL-754 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Operations, Maintenance, Safety & Analytics (PA-174.3).)
- CTL-754: PM schedule adherence (VS-138); climate-unit temp monitored; work-order closure verified
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (IFM), VS-35 (assets), VS-24 (HSE), VS-34 (procurement); W5037 (facility design), W5052 (fire/life-safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Climate-control-failure risk**: HVAC failure in climate units → tenant goods damage (mold/warp); mitigated by temp/humidity monitoring + rapid response
- **Deferred-PM risk**: Deferred door/lock PM → security gaps; mitigated by PM schedule adherence
- **Pest risk**: Infestation → tenant complaints/claims; mitigated by integrated pest management (VS-138)
System Touchpoints: - IFM/CMMS work-order (VS-138); storage PMS site ops; HSE (VS-24); asset/fixed-asset (VS-35); vendor/maintenance procurement (VS-34)

steps.activity: Run daily site operations: open/close, lighting/HVAC/climate-control checks (climate units), corridor/elevator/lift function, signage, and the daily walk-through
Execute housekeeping & PM: cleaning, pest control (links VS-138), door/lock/roller-door lubrication, lighting replacement, and the scheduled PM cycle on facility assets
Manage reactive maintenance: tenant-reported defects, work-order creation, vendor dispatch, and closure verification feeding facilities analytics (VS-138)

fields.Participants: Security/LP (VS-23/VS-159), IT (VS-27), Property Manager, HSE (VS-24), police liaison

workflows.name: Storage Security Operations, Surveillance, Access System & Incident Response

Automation Opportunity: - AI-video analytics (intrusion/loitering detection); alarm→guard auto-dispatch; system-health monitoring
Controls: - CTL-754 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Operations, Maintenance, Safety & Analytics (PA-174.3).)
- CTL-754: CCTV/access uptime SLA; incident evidence retained (VS-88); LP case managed (VS-23); claims Insurance-coordinated (VS-26)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23/VS-159 (security/LP), VS-27 (access IT), VS-26 (insurance), VS-88 (retention); W5043 (access control), W5049 (facility ops)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Theft-loss risk**: Break-in/theft → tenant loss & claims; mitigated by layered security + response
- **System-outage risk**: CCTV/access downtime → blind period; mitigated by uptime SLA + PM
- **Claim-exposure risk**: Inadequate evidence → denied defense/claim; mitigated by evidence retention (VS-88)
System Touchpoints: - CCTV/VMS (VS-23/VS-159); access-control/gate (VS-27); LP case management (VS-23); insurance/claims (VS-26); evidence retention (VS-88); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Operate surveillance & access system health: CCTV/VMS uptime, access-control/gate system availability, door-alarm monitoring, and the security-system PM (links VS-27/VS-23)
Respond to incidents: theft/break-in, unit-alarm, after-hours loitering, vehicle incident — dispatch guard/LP/police, secure the scene, and document
Investigate & report: LP case management (VS-23), tenant-claim handling with Insurance (VS-26), CCTV evidence retention (VS-88), and recurring-incident analytics

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Property Manager, Legal (VS-100), Security (VS-23), Compliance (VS-22)
fields.Trigger: Move-in (W5042); periodic inspection; suspected prohibited storage

Automation Opportunity: - Prohibited-goods acknowledgment e-capture; inspection scheduling; AI-video anomaly flagging on visible items
Controls: - CTL-754: prohibited-goods policy in lease & acknowledged (W5038); inspection right exercised; hazardous disposal per VS-73/VS-114
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-114 (DG/hazmat), VS-73 (waste), VS-100 (legal); W5038 (lease), W5042 (move-in), W5052 (fire/life-safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire/safety risk**: Flammables/LPG/fuels stored → fire/explosion (links W5052); mitigated by inspection & enforcement
- **Legal/liability risk**: Illegal items on premises; mitigated by inspection right + authority reporting
- **Hazardous-disposal risk**: Improper handling of discovered hazardous goods (DENR); mitigated by VS-73/VS-114 protocol
System Touchpoints: - Storage PMS inspection record; HSE (VS-24); lease/termination (VS-100/W5038); hazardous-waste disposal (VS-73/VS-114); compliance (VS-22)
Time Estimate: - ~15–30 min/move-in briefing; periodic inspection ~per site cycle

steps.activity: Communicate prohibited-goods policy: at lease execution (W5038/W5042), brief the tenant on the prohibited list (flammables, explosives, fuels/LPG, perishables, illegal items, hazardous waste) and the inspection right
Inspect & enforce: periodic visual inspections, investigate suspected prohibited storage, and enforce removal/termination per lease for violations
Handle hazardous discovery: if hazardous/illegal items found, coordinate safe removal/disposal (DENR/links VS-73), legal termination, and reporting to authorities if required

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Facilities (VS-138), BFP/fire consultant, Property Manager, Security (VS-23), BC/DR (VS-26)
fields.Trigger: Facility build/commission (W5037); annual FSIC renewal; drill cycle; incident

workflows.name: Storage Fire/Life-Safety, BFP Compliance & Emergency Preparedness

Automation Opportunity: - Fire-system IoT monitoring → auto-alert/Suppression; FSIC-renewal calendar auto-trigger (VS-166)
Controls: - CTL-754: BFP FSIC current (VS-166); fire-system PM (VS-138); prohibited flammables enforced (W5051); incident reported to BFP/DOLE
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-26 (BC/DR), VS-69 (disaster), VS-138 (IFM), VS-166 (permits); W5037 (design), W5051 (prohibited goods)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire-spread risk**: Flammable stored goods + partition failure → rapid fire spread (links W5051); mitigated by BFP-compliant design + suppression + prohibited-goods enforcement
- **FSIC-lapse risk**: Lapsed FSIC → BFP closure/penalty; mitigated by permit calendar (VS-166)
- **Tenant-safety risk**: Emergency response gaps; mitigated by drills + comms
System Touchpoints: - Fire alarm/suppression system; BFP FSIC register (VS-166); HSE/OSH (VS-24); BC/DR (VS-26); facility/CMMS (VS-138); LGU permit (VS-166)
Time Estimate: - ~annual FSIC cycle; ~quarterly drills; per-incident as needed

steps.activity: Maintain fire/life-safety systems: detection/suppression (sprinkler/extinguisher/hydrant), fire-rated partitions, egress, signage, and the annual BFP Fire Safety Inspection & FSIC (links VS-166)
Run emergency preparedness: evacuation plan, fire/earthquake/typhoon drills (links VS-69), and tenant emergency communication
Respond & report incidents: fire/smoke/gas incident response, BFP/DOLE/authority reporting, and BC/DR activation for major events (VS-26)

fields.Participants: Logistics (VS-06), Facilities (VS-138), Property Manager, Procurement (VS-34), Finance (VS-35)

workflows.name: Portable Container Fleet Maintenance, Cleaning, Sanitization & Lifecycle

Automation Opportunity: - GPS container tracking; return→clean→ready status workflow; asset-reconciliation automation
Controls: - CTL-754 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Operations, Maintenance, Safety & Analytics (PA-174.3).)
- CTL-754: clean/sanitize gate before re-rental; container asset reconciled (VS-111/VS-35); condemnation/disposal per VS-34/VS-35
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (fleet), VS-111 (RTI/asset), VS-35 (fixed asset), VS-34 (disposal), VS-138 (CMMS); W5036 (fleet strategy), W5045 (delivery/return), W5046 (inspection)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Re-rent-contaminated risk**: Re-renting unclean/damaged container → tenant complaint/health; mitigated by clean/sanitize gate before re-rental
- **Asset-drift risk**: Containers lost across the network; mitigated by GPS + asset reconciliation (VS-111)
- **Over-retention risk**: Holding condemned containers; mitigated by lifecycle disposal
System Touchpoints: - Container-asset tracking (VS-111/VS-06/VS-35); fleet/maintenance (VS-06); CMMS (VS-138); procurement/disposal (VS-34); fixed-asset (VS-35)

steps.activity: Receive & inspect returned containers: check structural integrity (doors/lock-box/floor/wind-water-tight), damage (links W5046), and quarantine damaged units
Clean, sanitize & repair: pressure-wash/sanitize, deodorize, repair doors/lock-box/vents, and certify wind/water-tight before re-rental
Manage lifecycle & redeployment: rebalance across sites per demand (W5055), retire/condemn beyond-economical-repair units, and update the container-asset register (VS-35/VS-111)

fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), FP&A (VS-17.4), Director Storage, Property Manager, Yield Mgmt (W5039)

workflows.name: Storage Occupancy, Revenue, Delinquency & Yield Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Automated PMS→BI feed; RevPAU/occupancy live dashboards; churn-risk scoring
Controls: - CTL-754 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Operations, Maintenance, Safety & Analytics (PA-174.3).)
- CTL-754: KPIs reconciled to O2C/FP&A (VS-16/VS-17.4); delinquency/bad-debt consistent with provisions
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-13 (CRM), VS-16 (O2C); W5035 (pricing), W5039 (yield), W5055 (forecast), W5056 (program perf)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-blindness risk**: Operating without occupancy/yield visibility → reactive mismanagement; mitigated by the KPI model
- **Mis-attribution risk**: Churn mis-attributed (price vs service vs access); mitigated by cohort/driver analysis
- **Lag risk**: Slow reporting → missed intervention window; mitigated by weekly cycles
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI/data warehouse (VS-28); storage PMS feed; FP&A (VS-17.4); CRM/loyalty (VS-13); O2C (VS-16)

steps.activity: Build the storage KPI model: physical & economic occupancy, street-vs-in-place rate, RevPAU, tenant lifetime value (LTV), acquisition cost (CAC), delinquency %, bad-debt %, churn
Diagnose performance: site-level benchmarking, cohort analysis (move-in source/term/discount), churn-driver analysis, and delinquency root-cause
Drive action: feed insights to yield (W5039), pricing (W5035), marketing/retention (VS-14), and program strategy (W5056); close-the-loop with FP&A (VS-17.4)

fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), Yield Mgmt (W5039), Fleet (VS-06/W5036), Marketing (VS-14), S&OP (VS-127)
fields.Trigger: Planning cycle; seasonality (summer move, year-end, post-disaster); fleet sizing

Automation Opportunity: - Time-series demand model; weather/disaster-surge scenario planning; fleet-rebalancing recommendations
Controls: - CTL-754 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Operations, Maintenance, Safety & Analytics (PA-174.3).)
- CTL-754: forecast reconciled to actuals (W5054); capacity within capex envelope (VS-35); feeds S&OP (VS-127)
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-127 (S&OP), VS-06 (fleet), VS-69 (disaster); W5036 (fleet), W5039 (yield), W5054 (actuals)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stock-out risk**: Under-forecasting demand → lost rentals/waitlist; mitigated by seasonality modeling
- **Over-capacity risk**: Over-building fleet/units → stranded assets; mitigated by demand-driven sizing
- **Disaster-blindness risk**: Post-disaster storage surge unmet (VS-69); mitigated by disaster-scenario planning
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/forecasting (VS-28); storage PMS; S&OP/IBP (VS-127); fleet (VS-06); CRM lead pipeline (VS-13)

steps.activity: Forecast demand: model move-in/move-out seasonality (summer/holiday/post-disaster VS-69), renovation/project cycles, and external drivers (housing, disasters)
Plan capacity & fleet: translate demand into unit availability, container fleet positioning (W5053), and staffing/marketing timing
Reconcile & refine: compare forecast to actual (W5054), feed S&OP/IBP (VS-127) where storage capacity is a constraint, and refine the model

workflows.name: Storage Program Performance, ROI & Cross-Sell/Basket-Linkage Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Storage↔merchandise transaction linkage (member ID); ROI dashboard; scenario/planning model
Controls: - CTL-754 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Operations, Maintenance, Safety & Analytics (PA-174.3).)
- CTL-754: program P&L reconciled to FP&A (VS-17.4); capex within VS-35/VS-40 envelope; cross-sell measured consistently
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-28 (analytics), VS-33 (strategy), VS-13 (loyalty), VS-143/VS-162 (large-item attach), VS-43 (trade-pro); W5033 (strategy), W5039 (yield), W5054 (KPIs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-capex risk**: Under-performing sites not exited; mitigated by site-level ROI review
- **Cross-sell-blindness risk**: Storage viewed in isolation vs its basket-lift contribution; mitigated by linkage analytics
- **Strategic-drift risk**: Program not adapting to demand; mitigated by annual strategy refresh (W5033)
System Touchpoints: - FP&A (VS-17.4); analytics/BI (VS-28); CRM/loyalty cross-sell (VS-13); O2C (VS-16); capex (VS-35/VS-40); strategy (VS-33)

steps.activity: Measure program ROI: NOI, capex payback, recurring-revenue contribution, and the program P&L vs business case (W5033)
Quantify cross-sell/basket-linkage: storage-tenant merchandise attach (VS-143/VS-162 large items), renovation-basket linkage, and trade-pro storage usage (VS-43); measure dwell/basket lift
Recommend & steer: site expansion/pause/exit, pricing/yield adjustments (W5039), and portfolio rebalancing — feeding the strategy cycle (W5033) and capital plan (VS-35/VS-40)
